transcript: You wouldn't expect a world famous supermodel to live in a slump, but this girl does. Hi, I'm Malisha. I'm a supermodel from Mumbai. And she told me something I can't stop thinking about. She's been on the cover of Vogue and Cosmopolitan magazine, worked with some of the world's biggest fashion brands, and she's only 17 years old. She grew up homeless near the boardwalk. The government comes and they break our house. How many times in your life has it happened? Maybe 12 times. To help her family get by, Malisha used to sell tissues on the street to strangers. How much did you earn in a month? Maybe 400. Until one day she met the stranger who would change her life. There was a foreigner, then he told me that what do you want to become? And he said that I can make you model. Malisha doesn't fit into the same box as most models. I don't do makeup. Most models are opposite. You're different. I know. Malisha has accomplished things that she would only dream of. But the thing that really blew my mind is how she sees her newfound fame. I don't think I'm pretty, but I thank God for everything. Like I have hands, I have mouth to speak. So I think I'm blessed.
metadata_caption: She's Been On The Vogue Cover But Lives In A Slum
